core_obligations: Prove the module-level identity (proof lines 3746-3752): for an O-module F and an O'-module G one has F tensor_O f^*G = F tensor over f^{-1}O' with f^{-1}G, because f^*G is by definition O tensor over f^{-1}O' with f^{-1}G and the tensor product is associative over the intermediate sheaf of rings.

Pass to complexes (proof lines 3752-3754): the author records that the lemma for complexes F^bullet and G^bullet follows from this module-level identity together with the definitions, that is, by representing the objects of the derived category and using the definition of the derived tensor product; the identity is compatible with the passage to derived tensor products.
Read off the bifunctoriality (statement with the proof): the identity is canonical and functorial in both variables, which is what the statement asserts.
proof_roadmap: Unfold the definition of f^*G as O tensor over f^{-1}O' with f^{-1}G.
Use associativity of the tensor product over the intermediate sheaf of rings to identify the two expressions.
Pass to complexes by the definitions of the derived tensor product.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states a variant of the derived projection formula, identifying F^bullet tensor^L_O Lf^*G^bullet with F^bullet tensor^L over f^{-1}O' of f^{-1}G^bullet (statement lines 3727-3743). The proof is short and proceeds by unfolding definitions: for modules the identity F tensor_O f^*G = F tensor over f^{-1}O' of f^{-1}G follows from the definition of f^*G as O tensor over f^{-1}O' of f^{-1}G together with associativity of the tensor product (proof lines 3746-3752), and the author records that the case of complexes follows from this and the definitions of the derived tensor product (proof lines 3752-3754). The content is the correct unfolding, which is why the argument is one line. The claim is H2: a definitional identification, with the passage to complexes stated as following from the definitions.
